subject: Re: [stan-users] Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!
parts:
Yes, your transformed parameter block is not right.
You are trying to define Z[n] for n in 1:N, but instead
loop twice on Ncam0, which is leaving at least one of the Z[n]
undefined and presumably defining and redefining many of the
other Z[n].

I have no idea what your intention is, so I don't have a suggested
fix.

- Bob


> On Sep 29, 2016, at 6:58 AM, Dung Tran <trungd...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I am modifying the codes in Section 6.14 to model a binary variable. The idea is use latent normal. Since I would like to extend to the case of multivariate outcomes from binary, ordinal, and continuous variables (mixed outcomes), so I try to use latent ones.
>
> For this post, I try one binary for easily to build up later.
>
> I run the following codes:
>
> data {
> int<lower=1> N; // Sample size
> int<lower=0, upper=1> Cam[N]; // Response
>
> int<lower=0> NCam0;
> int<lower=0> NCam1;
> int indCam[N];
>
> real Age[N]; // Predictor: Age
> }
>
> parameters {
> vector[2] beta; // Regression parameters
> vector<upper=0>[NCam0] Z0; // Latent
> vector<lower=0>[NCam1] Z1; // Latent
> }
>
> transformed parameters {
> real Z[N];
>
> for (i in 1: NCam0){
> Z[indCam[i]] = Z0[i];
> }
>
> for (i in 1: NCam0){
> Z[indCam[NCam0+i]] = Z1[i];
> }
> }
>
> model {
>
> for (j in 1:2){
> beta[j] ~ normal(0, 100); // Prior distribution for beta
> }
>
> for (i in 1 : N){
> Z[i] ~ normal(beta[1] + beta[2]*Age[i], 1);
> }
> }
>
> The idea here is: Latent Z is composed of Z0 and Z1 where Z0 is equivalent to response =0 and Z1 when response =1. Note that Z0 is <0 and Z1 is >0 (0 is the cuttpoint).
>
> However I got the error: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan! The error points to the line command: Z[i] ~ normal(beta[1] + beta[2]*Age[i], 1).
>
> Do you have any idea?
>
> Thank,
> Tran.
>
